title: fix(plugin-detail): three sibling record blocks read `requiredPermissions` as an ADR-0066 capability set, fail-closed (objectui#10155)
body:
Fixes #10155

Clause-②: no

Clause-②-correction: declared here FROM THE DIFF, as the claim comment (id `5751742067`) said it would be — that comment deliberately carried no `Clause-②:` line because there was no diff yet. Derivation: this package publishes one entry (its `package.json` `exports` has a single `.` condition set over `dist/index`), the diff adds no `export` to any `src/` file, and the one new file is a test under `__tests__/` that the published entry never reaches. No schema key, no closed-set member, no registry entry.

Applies the shape PR objectui#10153 landed on `record:quick_actions` to the three sibling record blocks that carried the identical call, byte for byte: `record:details`, `record:highlights` and `record:related_list`. The shape was settled there and is copied here, not re-invented.

## Step 1 — the GRADE question, answered

The card asks whether these blocks' actions are **independently refused server-side**, because the grade is `p1` only if they are. It is answerable from `objectstack-ai/objectstack`, read-only, and the answer is **yes — nothing on these three surfaces is authorised by this client gate**. The grade stays `p1`.

Three readings, each from that repository:

1. **There is no action-invoke route on the REST server at all.** `rest-route-ledger.ts`'s `data-actions` family carries the sentence "THERE IS NO ACTION-INVOKE ROUTE IN THIS FAMILY, AND ITS ABSENCE IS DELIBERATE", and records a QA probe that measured four candidate spellings answering 404 against a booted showcase. So "`requiredPermissions` is not enforced over REST" is a surface that does not exist, not a hole.
2. **Where an action's own `requiredPermissions` IS enforced:** `actionPermissionError` in `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`, reached on the platform path — the runtime dispatcher's `/actions` domain, which refuses with 403 under the comment "[ADR-0066 D4] Dual-surface action gate — the server is the source of truth", and the MCP `run_action` bridge. It is **fail-closed**: it reads `new Set(ec?.systemPermissions ?? [])`, so an unreported or absent capability set holds nothing and every declared capability is missing; only `ec.isSystem` bypasses. ⚠️ Note the deliberate asymmetry with this repo: the server treats "unreported" as **deny**, the UI treats it as **unknown, show** (objectui#4656). That is the correct direction for both.
3. **The DATA these three blocks display** is admitted by the engine middleware's object-read gate. `ISecurityService.canReadObject`'s contract docblock describes that gate arm for arm, naming "the ADR-0066 D3 `requiredPermissions` capability AND-gate" among them, and states "**Fails CLOSED.**" That is the reading the filing seat already had; reading 1 and 2 are the action-invocation half it correctly said was still open.

⇒ this block-level gate is **presentational**. It hides or shows a block and authorises nothing. The defect is a declared gate that silently does not gate — and the UI's refusal node reads as proof the rule is being kept — which is serious, but it is not privilege escalation.

⚠️ One honest edge, stated rather than smoothed: reading 2 gates on an ACTION's own `requiredPermissions`. An action that declares none is allowed by `actionPermissionError` by design (it returns `null` for an empty set). An author who tried to gate such actions with the BLOCK-level key alone would have no server-side refusal behind them — but a client-side gate never was an authorisation, before or after this change, so this does not move the grade.

## The three relayed measurements, re-derived here

The filing seat filed this card itself, so its readings carry no second opinion. All three were re-run on this branch's base.

| Relayed | Reproduced? |
|---|---|
| `record-details.tsx`, `record-highlights.tsx` and `record-related-list.tsx` each evaluate `requiredPermissions` through `required.every((p) => perms.can(objectName, p as any))` | **yes**, all three, and the same grep returns the repaired `record-quick-actions.tsx` site as PROSE forbidding the call |
| `record-related-list.tsx` does not carry the `&& objectName` guard the others have | **yes as written, but the consequence does not follow** — see below |

⭐ **The correction.** The `&& objectName` conjunct really is absent from `record-related-list.tsx`'s gate, but that site does not have the fail-open the other two have, and it never did: its `objectName` comes from `schema.objectName`, and the branch that renders the "record:related_list — missing objectName" placeholder returns **before** the gate is reached. So the "second silent fail-open" is real on `record:details` and `record:highlights` and is **not** a reading that ever applied to the related list. Pinned in both directions rather than left as prose.

## What changed

Each of the three now reads `perms.hasCapabilities(required)` — the permission context's ADR-0066 capability path over the reported `systemPermissions` — and gates fail-closed. The object name leaves the verdict at all three sites, because a system capability is not object-scoped.

`record-highlights.tsx` also carried a comment asserting the wrong reading outright — that `requiredPermissions` is a list "which all must pass on the active object". It is replaced with the code, not left standing over a repaired call. `record-details.tsx` carried a second stale mention of the old call inside its rules-of-hooks narrative; that is repaired too.

**Two calls deliberately do NOT move.**

- `record-related-list.tsx`'s automatic child-object read gate still asks the object-action path about `read` — one of the stock provider's eight mapped verbs, resolving to that object's own `allowRead` bit, which is the question it means to ask. It is pinned in place, both verdicts.
- `can()` and `hasCapabilities` themselves are untouched, and no other caller moves.

**The residual this accepts and states.** A provider that never REPORTS capabilities (`systemPermissions` absent — the role-based `PermissionProvider`, or a backend predating ADR-0066) still opens these gates. That is `hasCapabilities`'s own ruled unreported-vs-empty doctrine (objectui#4656), shared with every capability gate in the tree, and moving it is not this card's to do. A REPORTED empty array is a real answer and gates strictly.

## Pins — 46, all on real stock providers

New file: `record-blocks.requiredPermissions-gate.test.tsx`, one harness over all three blocks.

⚠️ **The mocked-`usePermissions` disease, checked before extending anything.** Of the three renderers, only `record:details` had any pin naming this key at all — `record-details.test.tsx`, whose subject is the rules-of-hooks contract (React error #310), not the gate. It **did** carry the disease: its `usePermissions` was mocked down to `{ can: () => stub.can }`, so it pinned the gate as an object-action read. `record:highlights` and `record:related_list` had **no** pin on this key at all, in any file. So there was nothing to rewrite for two of the three, and for the third the right repair was not a rewrite: that file's subject is hook ordering, so its double now answers the capability path and says in its own docblock that it pins nothing about the gate's semantics.

Every pin in the new file mounts a real `MePermissionsProvider` or a real role-based `PermissionProvider`. The only test double is a **delegating** spy that records what the object-permission path was asked without changing any answer — a mock that ANSWERS cannot discriminate the two reading paths, it IS whichever path the mock implements.

Per block, all three: reported-empty capability set hides · capability held renders · unknown name hides · empty array renders · absent key renders · partial grant of a two-element array hides, all granted renders · **DISCRIMINATOR ①** `allowRead: true` plus an empty capability set hides · **DISCRIMINATOR ③** the enum member `manage` is gated rather than resolved to the read bit · **DETECTOR** the renderer never asks the object-permission path about a capability name · role-based provider with and without an object config, same verdict.

**DISCRIMINATOR ②** is per block, because it cannot be spelled identically on all three:

- `record:details` and `record:highlights` — capability held with `allowRead: false` **renders**. Opposite inputs to ①, opposite verdict, so neither can pass on a gate that is simply always-open or always-closed.
- `record:related_list` — its automatic object-read gate refuses an `allowRead: false` object one branch earlier, so its ② is pinned on `allowRead: true`, and the `allowRead: false` leg is pinned separately as the object-read call this card must not move.

Plus: `record:details` and `record:highlights` gate with NO objectName in the record context; `record:related_list` answers its missing-objectName placeholder **before** the gate, which is the corrected reading above; and a **CONTROL** transcribing both stock providers' full 13-name `can()` truth table, pinned as UNCHANGED including the verdicts that are the defect itself.

⭐ The DETECTOR pins assert a negative, and a negative alone passes on a spy that never fires. The related-list object-read pins assert the spy DOES fire, with `('crm_contact', 'read')`, and are this file's proof that it is wired.

## Ablation

Committed first. Then the three renderers alone were checked out at their base blobs and each verified **on disk by hash** against the expected base blob, with an `EXIT INT TERM` trap holding absolute restore paths; the mutated text was counted in both directions on disk before the run (capability gate 1 to 0, object-action gate 0 to 1, per file). No build step is involved: the pins import these renderers by relative path within the same package, so the mutation cannot fail to reach them.

```
ABLATION  → Test Files  2 failed (2) | Tests  25 failed | 24 passed (49)
RESTORED  → all three blobs back to their HEAD blobs, `git diff HEAD` empty
```

The 25 that went red: 6 per block times 3 blocks (the empty-set pin, unknown name, partial grant, ① , ③ and the DETECTOR), plus the role-based "WITH an object permission config" leg on `record:details` and `record:highlights`, plus ② and the no-objectName pin on those same two, plus the rules-of-hooks permission-flip pin in `record-details.test.tsx`.

**The 24 that stayed green are the controls**, and that is the load-bearing half: both `can()` truth tables, the absent key, the empty array, the all-granted positive control, the capability-held pin, the role-based WITHOUT-config leg, and all three of `record:related_list`'s object-read pins including its missing-objectName placeholder. The truth tables staying green on both legs is the evidence that they pin `can()` and not this gate.

⚠️ Two ablated legs are reported as they measured rather than as a template would predict. The role-based "WITH an object permission config" leg went red on two blocks of three, not three: `record:related_list` reads its CHILD object, which carries no config in either arm of that pair, so pre-fix it answered the same way with and without. And `record:related_list`'s ② could not be given hostile object bits for the reason stated above.

## Checks on this head

Run at `adee5d46a`, which is this branch after `origin/main` was merged in (merge, never rebase).

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `packages/plugin-detail` full suite (repo-root vitest, under the shared verify lock) | **193 files / 1960 tests passed** |
| `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/__tests__/` re-run on the merged head | **53 files / 611 tests passed** |
| `turbo run type-check --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail` with its build closure | **13 tasks successful, exit 0** — and this package's `type-check` runs `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` as a second pass, so the new pins are type-checked, not excluded |
| `eslint .` in `packages/plugin-detail` | **exit 0 — 251 files, 0 errors**, 1065 pre-existing warnings |
| `check:changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major` | pass — 1 changeset for 5 published source files |
| `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:test-path-roots` | pass |
| `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape` | pass |
| `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals` | pass (both report-only) |
| `check:component-surface-parity`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:element-data-source-declaration`, `check:self-import`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:unused-deps`, `check:registry-bare-names` | pass |
| `check:sdui-registration-pins`, `check:eager-closure` | **NOT MEASURED locally** — both exit 2 with their prerequisite-not-met arm ("No console build to weigh"), which is not a budget failure. CI owns them. |

Control bytes were also scanned directly over the changed files with a Unicode-class grep, beyond the gate: no hits.

**Lint narrowing, declared.** The repo-wide lint run belongs to CI; this PR ran the affected package instead. Three readings make that a measurement rather than a gap: ① the population is eslint's own — the package's `lint` script is `eslint .`, so the config decides what is linted, not a guess of mine; ② the 251-file count is read from eslint's `--format json` output; ③ this config enables **no type-aware linting** — there is no `parserOptions.project` and no `projectService` anywhere in `eslint.config.js` — so a file's verdict depends only on its own bytes and the config, and this diff moves neither for any untouched file. `lint.yml` sets no max-warnings, and every ratchet rule in this config is per-file with no tree-wide baseline a scoped run could miss.

**Bundle Analysis.** Nothing in `check-eager-closure-budget.mjs` or any ceiling was touched. This diff adds no import and no new eager module — it changes one expression per renderer plus comments and tests — so it moves no chunk.

## Acceptance notes — out of scope here

**Noted, not filed.** `apps/console`'s registry-inputs spec-parity ledger narrates objectui#8071's fourth slice and quotes the block-level gate's source as `required.every((p) => perms.can(objectName, p))`. That quotation described `record:quick_actions`, which PR objectui#10153 already moved off that call, so the paragraph now quotes a source line that no longer exists anywhere in the tree. It is a historical accounting note rather than a live claim, and repairing it means editing a package this PR does not otherwise touch, which the opportunistic-repair rule says not to do as a sweep. Who would meet it: whoever next adjudicates that ledger's `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTIONS` accounting.

**Noted, not filed.** The card records a SECOND subject with its own dedupe words — the two capability paths that can disagree, `perms.hasCapabilities` versus `useCapabilityGate`. It is already written down on the card for triage to split out; nothing is added here.

## Not measured

CI convergence. This body is published at local-check completion; the gates above are this head's real readings, and anything that reds afterwards comes back as a patch on the same claim.
